five of the six sketches differ from 9p1p1's in what they hold on to, and they differ the same way. Where 9p1p1 constrains to the sketch's own origin, these sketches constrain to ids in the part studio's space, picked off the screen; and in the one sketch where 9p1p1 reaches out to the model, torso shoulder profile, this tab reaches for the same geometry without projecting it. Nothing is wrong with the model: the dimensions, the planes and the solid all match. What differs is what the sketches say about why the model is that shape, which is the thing this run exists to get right, so it goes to Mike with the shoulder region question.

three sketches carry one constraint more than 9p1p1's does: hip connector location an extra coincident, neck connector location a second coincident, trim shoulder pattern a second vertical. Each is what it costs to pin a point against two things picked off the screen where one origin would have done. Onshape solves all three, so none is over-constrained; each is still a constraint the guide would have to tell a reader to make.
